## Two different questions, not two versions of the same one

A standard soil test answers one precise question: which nutrients are available, and in what amount. It's a chemical reading, essential for adjusting a season's fertilization plan. A soil health diagnostic asks a broader question: is this soil actually functioning well, physically and biologically, not just chemically. These are complementary tools, not two ways of answering the same question.

## What a soil health diagnostic adds

A model calibrated specifically for Quebec conditions, published in 2023 in the *Canadian Journal of Soil Science* (Gauthier et al.), evaluates 15 indicators across three categories. The physical component looks at aggregate stability and available water capacity, two measures of soil structure. The biological component looks at microbial respiration and potentially mineralizable nitrogen, indicators of the soil's living activity. The chemical component covers the usual nutrients — pH, phosphorus, potassium, and several others.

## Why structure and biology matter too

A soil can show adequate chemical values and still underperform, because its structure limits root development or because its biological activity is low. These blind spots don't show up on a standard fertility certificate, but they often explain yield gaps that a purely chemical reading can't account for.

## What the protocol actually requires

The model was calibrated on a precise sampling method: a shovel, 0 to 20 cm deep, taken at several representative points within a homogeneous zone of the field. [Targeting that sampling](../echantillonnage-cible-sol/index.qmd) on the field's most relevant zones, rather than a general average, sharpens its practical value. A compaction reading is taken directly on site, in addition to the sample sent to the lab. This isn't a loose variation on a standard soil test — it's a fixed protocol, because the model's validity depends on it.

## What it doesn't replace

A soil health diagnostic isn't a full pedological soil profile — it doesn't describe soil horizons in a pit. It's a targeted picture of specific functional indicators, not an exhaustive characterization of the profile.
